da-vacuous.evidence: conj-qbeta-c-k-closed-forms.lean:98-101 theorem qbeta_c_k_closed_forms_derived (q) : ∃ c_4 c_5, c_4 = -2*(hoefsmitB q)^4 ∧ c_5 = -((hoefsmitB q)^2+1/2) := sorry
da-vacuous.notes: The headline 'derived' theorem is vacuous as stated: ∃ c_4 c_5 with those exact defining equalities is trivially true (witness the RHS, prove by ⟨_,_,rfl,rfl⟩) — it asserts the values exist, NOT that they are derived from the categorical Markov trace. It is marked `sorry` despite being provable without effort, and its name ('..._derived') promises a first-principles derivation the statement cannot express. Either way the declaration carries no derivation content: vacuous-existence dressed as a derivation theorem (AGENTS.md §1a anti-pattern).

da-circular.evidence: conj-qbeta-c-k-closed-forms.md:83-86 "empirical c_k from binding_q_target_sweep are NOT arbitrary fits — they are TAUTOLOGICALLY determined by the precision-ladder structure applied to CODATA Q_β"
da-circular.notes: Mild circular framing: the c_k are extracted by matching the ladder product to the CODATA Q_β value, then the same CODATA-anchored extraction is cited as evidence the forms are 'tautologically determined' rather than fitted. The closed forms (−2·b^4, etc.) are post-hoc pattern guesses for those CODATA-derived numbers; calling them 'not fits' because the extraction is forced is a definitional sleight — the closed-FORM identification remains a fit (residuals 0.9–114%).
